newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Infratil Int says AGI out of Argentine airport bid.
newsitem.headline: Infratil Int says AGI out of Argentine airport bid.

text.p: Airport Group International Inc (AGI) has pulled out of a planned bid for the privatisation of Argentine airports, a director of its New Zealand shareholder Infratil International said on Wednesday.
Infratil International has an 11.8 percent stake in AGI.
Director Kevin O'Connor told Reuters AGI would no longer take part in the Argentine government's plans to sell a 30-year concession to operate 28 airports.
"AGI have announced that they do not plan to bid at this stage, but that substantial further airport opportunities remain in Europe, South America and Australia for AGI," O'Connor said.
He said AGI had pulled out of the Argentine bid to "concentrate on the furtherance of these other opportunities".

"There's a range of them. In Latin America there's Mexico, Uruguay and Chile; in Europe there's Duesseldorf and East Berlin and Lisbon; and in Australia there are airports including Adelaide, Coolangatta and Canberra," O'Connor said.
Last month Infratil International launched a prospectus aiming to raise NZ$50 million through a one for two rights issue to Infrastructure and Utilities Ltd shareholders.
Half of the raised capital is to be used to fund the purchase of the 11.8 percent stake in AGI.
United States-based Lockheed Martin Inc owns 39 percent of AGI.
Infratil International is managed by New Zealand-based merchant bankers Morrison & Co, who also manage Infratil NZ Ltd and are specialist advisers to the Infrastructure and utilities sector.
